risks.title: Benchmark optimization displaces product quality
risks.cause: Agents optimize for 100 terminal passes or visible fixtures instead of user value, failure behavior and independent readiness.
risks.consequence: A green benchmark ships an unusable, unsafe, unsupported or commercially unready product.
mitigations: Four independent gates with AND release logic
triggers: Benchmark pass cited to waive another gate
Denominator or oracle change after results
risks.contingency: Freeze qualification, mark affected results contaminated, return to product/benchmark design, and require human change approval.

risks.title: Prototype code is promoted as production architecture
risks.cause: The prototype contains working UI, tests and live narratives that appear cheaper to copy than re-specify.
risks.consequence: Unreviewed schema, renderer, executor and trust failures enter production with hidden coupling.
triggers: Prototype branch becomes a feature base
React Flow or JSON declared permanent without ADR
risks.contingency: Stop the feature, discard unauthorized promotion through a reviewed recovery plan, and re-specify the accepted outcome from dev.

risks.title: Transport success is misrepresented as engineering correctness
risks.cause: MCP/application acceptance, artifact existence or syntactic parsing is easier to measure than engineering validity.
risks.consequence: Wright makes unsafe or false engineering claims and loses user trust.
triggers: Application accepted command but output not independently inspected
risks.contingency: Quarantine the case/claim, classify as benchmark-oracle failure, and obtain independent domain review.

review.cadence: Before any benchmark case is qualified

risks.title: Autonomy exceeds authority
risks.cause: A long-running coordinator treats program intent as permission for dependencies, external writes, credentials, paid systems, destructive actions or release.
risks.consequence: Unauthorized external mutation, cost, data exposure, legal risk or unsafe physical action.
mitigations: Explicit action charters and human gates
risks.contingency: Stop before action, preserve evidence and request exact scoped authority.

risks.title: Spec Kit singleton state targets the wrong feature
risks.cause: .specify/feature.json and the managed AGENTS.md pointer are shared mutable coordination files.
risks.consequence: One agent plans or implements another feature, corrupting scope and evidence.
mitigations: Verify singleton pointers after each command
Restore program pointer before dev integration
risks.contingency: Stop, audit both worktrees and return affected features to the last verified state.

review.cadence: Before and after every Spec Kit command

risks.title: Application-backed MCP has no authoritative subject
risks.cause: Multiple surfaces or stale clients can share a command queue while owning different in-memory engineering state.
risks.consequence: Inconsistent observations are retried until a desired result appears, destroying reproducibility and correctness.
triggers: Same run produces inconsistent application state
risks.contingency: Disable application-backed execution and retain deterministic/read-only functionality until a reviewed identity contract passes.

risks.title: Fixture output masquerades as current analysis
risks.cause: Scenario fixtures include convenient semantic findings and UI components can project them onto arbitrary input.
risks.consequence: False causal claims, unsafe recovery and severe user-trust failure.
risks.contingency: Stop execution integration, remove false result projection and add regression before resuming.

risks.title: Commercial readiness is claimed without an offering decision
risks.cause: Technical progress is described as production-ready despite current public-alpha/no-SLA policy and unverified external controls.
risks.consequence: Unsupported customer expectations, operational exposure and inaccurate marketing/release claims.
triggers: Unchecked external control treated as pass
risks.contingency: Block COMM-01 and release; correct claims and obtain approved offering/support evidence.

risks.title: Durable schema or interface strands historical state
risks.cause: A process/run/artifact/API change ships without reader ranges, migration, old-reader behavior or rollback proof.
risks.consequence: Users cannot open prior work or safely downgrade/recover.
risks.contingency: Block implementation/integration and redesign migration or narrow the feature to a non-persisted increment.

risks.title: Evidence and dashboard become stale or drift
risks.cause: Summaries are hand-edited or remain green after source, environment, oracle or candidate identity changes.
risks.consequence: Agents select invalid work and release decisions use obsolete evidence.
risks.contingency: Mark affected area stale, regenerate from source, and block transitions until reconciled.

review.cadence: Every state transition and dashboard generation

risks.title: Parallel WIP and CI thrash obscure causes
risks.cause: Multiple writers, broad changes, reruns and replacement pushes proceed before prior evidence is terminal.
risks.consequence: Conflicting mutations, repeated failures, token waste and unreliable attribution.
mitigations: Collect all CI failures before edit
risks.contingency: Stop mutation/pushes, freeze evidence, build one deterministic reproducer and request consolidated review.

risks.title: Proprietary data or reusable authority leaks through evidence
risks.cause: Run, benchmark, dashboard or support artifacts capture raw payloads, paths, credentials, commands, tokens or proprietary inputs/outputs.
risks.consequence: Security/privacy breach and unusable commercial evidence.
risks.contingency: Stop, contain/remove through an approved secret/proprietary-data incident process, invalidate exposed evidence and rotate authority if needed.

review.cadence: Before every commit, evidence publication and release

risks.title: New dependency or third-party asset is commercially unsuitable
risks.cause: Prototype popularity or technical fit is mistaken for current license, maintenance, vulnerability, redistribution and support suitability.
risks.consequence: Supply-chain, legal, bundle, platform or abandonment risk.
risks.contingency: Block feature, remove or replace dependency, and rerun architecture/packaging/license gates.

risks.title: Engineer usability is inferred from prototype screenshots/tests
risks.cause: The prototype human comprehension study remained incomplete while screenshots and component tests appear convincing.
risks.consequence: Dense or confusing workflows ship, especially at scale, narrow view or failure states.
risks.contingency: Keep product gate blocked, narrow UI claim and run the approved study before integration/release.

review.cadence: Before EPP-F02 integration and every material UX change

risks.title: Successful output has no usable lifetime or action
risks.cause: Runtime cleanup destroys session output or the UI exposes raw payload without a view/open/download/application contract.
risks.consequence: Green runs produce no actionable engineer outcome and cannot be reproduced or supported.
risks.contingency: Classify product run as failed/incomplete, retain safe evidence and redesign output delivery before release.

risks.title: Release surfaces diverge or completion is reported early
risks.cause: Candidates are rebuilt between validation/publication, registries diverge, native profiles are skipped, or merge/main checks are called a release.
risks.consequence: Users receive unverified artifacts and rollback/recovery cannot identify an immutable subject.
mitigations: Native lifecycle on all claimed platforms
risks.contingency: Leave release incomplete/draft, recover only with recorded immutable subjects or publish a corrected patch; never overwrite artifacts.

review.cadence: Every release rehearsal and production step

risks.title: Machine dashboard is mistaken for the required browser status experience
risks.cause: EPP-F01 generates dashboard.json and CLI reports while the original program outcome also requires a browser-accessible page; Wright's existing workspace landing dashboard looks adjacent but consumes different state.
risks.consequence: The program can report governance tooling complete while maintainers cannot see four-area readiness, 0-to-100 benchmark progress, active work, blockers, next action, evidence and freshness in the required accessible browser surface.
mitigations: Separate EPP-F01B after EPP-F01 and before EPP-F02
Keep browser projection read-only and evidence-derived
Test honest empty/stale/failed states and accessible traffic-light presentation
Require fresh exact approvals before EPP-F01 resumes
triggers: EPP-F02 becomes eligible before EPP-F01B integrates
risks.contingency: Keep EPP-F01 blocked, preserve validator WIP, and require a newly approved exact program subject; do not implement browser work inside EPP-F01 or claim the browser outcome complete.

review.cadence: Every EPP-F01/EPP-F01B transition and before EPP-F02 eligibility

risks.title: Committed-identity correction becomes a hidden waiver channel
risks.cause: A broad, editable, partial, or readiness-aware correction mechanism could be used to dispose unrelated control-plane, benchmark, approval, or release failures.
risks.consequence: Historical evidence appears valid without exact Git proof, independent readiness gates become coupled, and autonomous work or release can advance on waived defects.
mitigations: Require strict-ancestor Git-object recomputation and exact V4 approval binding
Retain original findings and reject corrections of corrections
Prove readiness, benchmark, freshness, approval and release non-interference
triggers: Wildcard/range or new correction target accepted
Correction changes any readiness area or release result
risks.contingency: Keep EPP-F01 and PROG-01/PROG-05 blocked, revoke the lease, preserve all original bytes, and require a new material decision rather than weakening validation.

review.cadence: Every EPP-F01 correction, compatibility, integration and release gate

risks.title: Transition input-origin correction becomes an authority bypass
risks.cause: A generic source/container exception could treat evidence created in a transition container as if it were available to authorize that transition.
risks.consequence: Append-only transition proof becomes circular and autonomous work may advance on authority that did not exist at the declared source.
mitigations: Require source absence and unique container introduction
Bind exact blobs and unchanged manifest
risks.contingency: Keep EPP-F01 and PROG-01/PROG-05 blocked, preserve original bytes, and require a new material decision rather than broadening the exception.

review.cadence: Every EPP-F01 transition-history, compatibility, integration and release gate
